context: The item is a second-hand phone, recently serviced.
transcript: Buyer ($60): A second-hand phone—even if 'serviced'—is a huge gamble and probably has a dying battery. I'm offering 60 for it, take it or I'll walk away right now.

Buyer ($100): Certified technician is just marketing talk to cover up delusional pricing for an outdated device. I can buy a brand new phone with a warranty for what you're asking, so 100 is my absolute limit or I walk right now.

Seller ($170): Brand new for a hundred bucks? You are living in a complete fantasy land! I am practically bleeding money here, but I will take 170 right now—grab this steal of a deal before I change my mind and kick you out!

Buyer ($120): Paying 170 for a used, questionable device with zero real warranty is ridiculous. It probably has hidden damage that your so-called technician masked. My final, generous counter is 120, or I am walking away right this second.

Seller ($170): Hidden damage?! You've got some nerve accusing me of being a cheat when I'm handing you absolute perfection on a silver platter! 120 is an utter joke, so 170 is my rock-bottom floor—pay up right now or get out of my sight!

Buyer ($130): You are completely delusional if you think anyone is paying 170 for a repaired lemon. I will squeeze my budget to give you 130, which is far more than generous for a device that could break tomorrow. Take 130 right now, or I am walking out that door for good.

Seller ($170): 130?! You are spitting in my face after I already dropped down to the absolute bone for you! 170 is my absolute rock-bottom floor, so hand over the cash right now or walk out that door!

Buyer ($130): 170 is a complete delusion for a second-hand risk like this. I am holding firm at 130, which is already more than this questionable hardware is worth. Accept 130 right now or watch me walk out that door for good.

Seller ($170): You are still holding firm at 130?! You must be deaf or completely blind to quality because I am NOT losing a single cent more on this pristine piece of tech! 170 is my final, absolute line in the sand—pay it right now or start walking, because you're wasting my damn time!

Buyer ($130): Keep your delusional 170 price tag and enjoy watching that overpriced brick gather dust on your shelf. My absolute ceiling is 130 for a risky, second-hand phone with zero guarantee. This is your last chance to take 130, or I am walking out the door for good.
Seller ($170): Then walk! I'd rather let this phone gather dust than let an ungrateful cheapskate rob me blind for 130! Hand over 170 right now or get out of my shop!

Buyer ($130): Fine, keep your overpriced paperweight! No one with half a brain is going to give you 170 for a risky, second-hand device. My absolute limit remains 130, so take it right now or I am walking out for good.
Seller ($170): Are you repeating yourself like a broken record now?! 130 is an absolute insult and you know it! Pay the 170 right now or get out of my face before I throw you out myself!
